triage_policy.likely_tp: Source is attacker-controllable inside nltk's own default data flow (network: XML index / package zip content / HTTP request path), OR the flow contains a genuine in-library escape primitive (a relative-name parameter joined onto a base without any containment check: find(resource_name), corpus fileid joins, creds_file join, zip entry names), AND the sink performs a real filesystem operation.
triage_policy.likely_fp: Sink is pure path construction (os.path.join / os.path.abspath - rubric Q3), or an effective fixed-value guard precedes the access, or the operation is exactly the documented authorized contract on the caller's own designated directory.
triage_policy.uncertain: Taint path and sink are real, but the only source is a caller-designated FULL-path public API parameter and the operation is that parameter's documented contract (write to outfile, save model to path, connect to dbname): exploitability depends entirely on the embedding application passing attacker-controlled values (the standard library-CVE pattern). No in-library escape primitive and no attacker channel within nltk's own usage.
triage_policy.note_on_library_model: The Pass-1 audited trust model (query_generation_notes.md section 2, consistent with the frozen labels) treats public API parameters as the application-facing boundary. That convention is respected below: such flows are not dismissed, they are recorded with their embedding-application precondition as either likely_tp (when an in-library join/escape primitive exists) or uncertain (when the parameter is a full path used per contract).

general_evidence.allowed_roots_q4: The project's implied roots are: the Downloader's download_dir (nltk_data dir), the nltk.data.path search dirs, and each CorpusReader's root. NONE is enforced at any use site - no startswith/relative_to/realpath containment check exists anywhere in the audited flows (verified by grep and first-hand reading).
general_evidence.traversal_factors_q5: os.path.join keeps '..' lexically and an absolute later component REPLACES the base (data.py:650/:657/:354, downloader.py:2281/:2287/:700/:709/:740); os.path.normpath preserves leading '../..' (data.py:257); url2pathname runs AFTER normalize_resource_name in find() (data.py:626 then :650/:657 - '%2e%2e%2f' decodes to '../' post-normalization, CWE-36 mixed-decoder ordering); unquote_plus decodes the wordnet HTTP request path (:99/:118); expanduser/join('~', pth) at twitter/util.py:152 lets a relative subdir escape the home dir; zip member names reach join(root, *pieces) unfiltered (downloader.py:2281/:2287). All of these genuinely change the final access target. Symlinks: no os.symlink in the tree; followlinks=True exists at corpus/reader/util.py:821 (not in this alert set); no realpath canonicalization anywhere.
general_evidence.barriers_q6_q7: The only effective guard in the whole alert set is wordnet_app.py:119 'usp == "NLTK Wordnet Browser Database Database Info.html"' exact literal equality, executed before the open at :122 (single fixed filename - effective whitelist of size 1). All other checks on the paths (os.path.exists/isfile/isdir at data.py:332/:651/:721, downloader.py:701/:707/:709/:743/:916, twitter/util.py:88, ipipan fileids membership) are existence probes that do not neutralize traversal. Nobody mistook normpath/abspath/exists/startswith for barriers: the labels model normpath/abspath as propagation (summary) and existence checks as role none - consistent with the first-hand source reading; the query's MySanitizers is none(), which is correct for this codebase.

rubric_answers_summary.q1_sources_attacker_controlled: Three real classes: (a) network - XML package-index attributes (downloader.py:286-288/:327-330, fetched via urlopen at :962) and downloaded package zip content (member names :2264, bytes :717-723); (b) wordnet_app.py:98 HTTP request path (network peer; but neutralized by the :119 literal guard); (c) public library API parameters (37 labels) - attacker-controllable only when the embedding application forwards untrusted values (library-CVE pattern). Findings 15/18/19/20/21/22/23/24/25 use class (a); 9-11/13/26/27/34/37 use genuine in-library join-escape primitives; the remainder are class (c) without escape primitives (uncertain).
rubric_answers_summary.q2_source_reaches_sink: Verified for all 38 alerts by first-hand reading: every codeFlow step corresponds to a real statement (Package field writes :230-:270, self._path :334, self._root api.py:97, _unzip_iter call :745, guess_path util.py:142-152, MTEFileReader/Framenet plumbing). No async calls on any path; the downloader coroutine yields are message plumbing that the alerts do not depend on. The handoff edges (kwargs expansion :288/:330, info.filename/info.subdir loads, constructor field loads) all match real assignments.
rubric_answers_summary.q3_real_sinks: 36/38 alerts anchor real filesystem operations (open/gzip.open/sqlite3.connect/ZipFile/OpenOnDemandZipFile/mkdir/remove/walk). 2 alerts are pure path-construction sinks and are triaged likely_fp: [12] data.py:506 (os.path.abspath argument) and [17] downloader.py:710 (os.path.join argument) - both documented same-line label artifacts (notes 6.5).
rubric_answers_summary.q4_allowed_roots: Implied roots: download_dir (nltk_data), nltk.data.path dirs, corpus reader roots, extraction root zipdir. None is enforced at any use site; no startswith/relative_to/realpath containment exists in the audited code.
rubric_answers_summary.q5_traversal_factors: All genuinely effective: leading-'..' preserved by normpath (data.py:257); absolute component replaces join base (data.py:650/:657/:354, downloader.py:2281/:2287/:700/:740); url2pathname decodes AFTER normalize (CWE-36 ordering hazard, data.py:650/:657); unquote_plus on the HTTP path (wordnet :118, but guard-gated); expanduser/join('~',...) escapes home (twitter/util.py:152); unfiltered zip member names (downloader.py:2281/:2287). No symlinks created anywhere; walk(followlinks=True) at corpus/reader/util.py:821 is outside this alert set.
rubric_answers_summary.q6_effective_guards: Exactly one effective guard exists in the alert set: wordnet_app.py:119 exact literal equality, executed at :118-:122 BEFORE the open - a fixed single-filename mapping. All other checks (exists/isfile/isdir/stat/fileids-membership) are existence probes occurring on the path but not confining it.
rubric_answers_summary.q7_mistaken_barriers: No. The query models normpath/abspath as propagation (summary) and existence checks as role none; MySanitizers is none() - consistent with the source. No startsWith-prefix or auth-only pseudo-barrier was credited anywhere.
rubric_answers_summary.q8_authorized_or_unreachable: [16]/[31] mkdir of the caller's own designated download/output dir (documented contract); [36] fixed-literal filename (and a local demo app); [0]/[1-4]/[14]/[28]/[29]/[30]/[32]/[33]/[35] caller-designated full-path parameters used per documented contract - kept uncertain (not dismissed) because the library-CVE pattern makes them exploitable only via the embedding application.
rubric_answers_summary.q9_fp_causes: Two documented same-line sink label artifacts ([12]/[17], notes 6.5); one expected guard-filter case ([36], Step-6 fixed-filename heuristic). No database-coverage or wrong-diagnostic-path FPs observed; no over-generalized sources beyond the documented candidate download_dir params.

ground_truth_analysis.task: Determine whether the real vulnerability (commit f59d7ed8df2e0e957f7f247fe218032abdbe9a10, CVE-2019-14751, CWE-22, nltk Downloader zip-slip in _unzip_iter) is hit by the formal Pass-1 alerts
ground_truth_analysis.vulnerable_code: nltk/downloader.py:2249-2300 _unzip_iter: namelist = zf.namelist() (:2264) -> filelist (:2271) -> loop filename (:2286) -> filepath = os.path.join(root, *filename.split('/')) (:2287) -> os.mkdir(dirpath) (:2283, dirpath from entry-name pieces :2281) -> open(filepath,'wb') + shutil.copyfileobj (:2290-2291). No filtering of entry names. The source snapshot in the database matches the pre-fix code_before exactly (verified line-by-line).
ground_truth_analysis.sink_hit: YES - alert [25] lands precisely on the vulnerable write primitive (join + open('wb') + copyfileobj) and alert [23] on the directory-creation half of the same primitive; both are inside _unzip_iter, which is reached from _download_package (:745) on every zip package download with unzip=True. The alerts correctly establish that no sanitization exists on this path (no entry-name filter, no containment check) - consistent with the CVE.
ground_truth_analysis.source_channel_fidelity: PARTIAL - the reported codeFlows for [22]/[23]/[25] taint the `root` operand (XML index `subdir` -> :740 zipdir = join(download_dir, info.subdir) -> :745 -> root; plus download_dir candidate params), NOT the canonical CVE source (zip member names from zf.namelist() at :2264, labeled source p1-s-046 = tp). The namelist source produced NO alert path: the chain namelist (:2264) -> dirlist/filelist comprehensions (:2265-:2271) -> enumerate loop unpacking (:2286) -> filename.split('/') -> *star-args into join (:2287) was not tracked by the analysis. The root-operand channel is nonetheless genuinely attacker-controllable under the same malicious-data-server trust model, so the alerts are true positives at the vulnerable sink, not coincidental FPs.
ground_truth_analysis.verdict: HIT at sink level: the formal Pass-1 result set contains likely_tp alerts at the exact vulnerable function and sink lines of CVE-2019-14751 (notably [25] downloader.py:2290). If the grading standard is 'the reported source->sink path reproduces the CVE's exact taint (member-name ../ -> arbitrary write)', the hit is partial: sink and primitive fully reproduced, source channel covered via the sibling XML-subdir/root operand while the namelist member-name channel (the CVE POC vector) itself generated no path - a source-to-sink coverage gap in this pass (candidate for a Pass-2 summary edge across the list comprehension / *args unpacking at :2287).
ground_truth_analysis.preconditions_for_the_reported_channel: attacker controls index.xml (subdir) - malicious mirror / compromised or attacker-chosen data server / victim pointed at an attacker URL; for the CVE's canonical channel, an attacker-crafted package zip (the historically accepted vector).
